domain: Japan-to-Korea vibe matching, plus food and omakase

kamakura_analogs.verdict: Busan east coast: Blueline Park Beach Train/Sky Capsule (Mipo-Cheongsapo-Songjeong) + Haedong Yonggungsa seaside temple + Cheongsapo lighthouse/skywalk + Huinnyeoul cliff village. Closest overall match: a little seaside train, a temple on rocks over the sea, small lanes and cafes, all inside a big city with omakase and hot springs nearby.

Yangyang Naksansa + Sokcho Abai Village/Jungang Market: the most 'spiritual seaside temple' match (cliff pavilion Uisangdae, 16 m Haesu Gwaneum statue facing the East Sea), plus a hand-pulled gaetbae raft and fishing-village food. Pairs with Seoraksan foliage in mid-late Oct. No coastal train, smaller town feel.

Gangneung: Anmok coffee street on the beach, Gyeongpo lake, Ojukheon Joseon house, Jeongdongjin seaside station (train station on the beach). Good small-city charm + chodang sundubu; temples are less central.
Tongyeong: 'Naples of Korea' harbor, Dongpirang hillside mural lanes, Hallyeosu cable car, oyster season starting. Charming but 4+ hours from Seoul and no rail; best as part of a south-coast loop.

Yeosu: Hyangiram hermitage on a sea cliff (very Kamakura/Enoshima), Odongdo island, romantic pojangmacha night harbor, sea cable car. Strong match but far from the Busan/Gyeongju/Seoul spine (2h50 KTX from Seoul).
Jeju Seogwipo: waterfalls, Olle trail coastal walks, Yakcheonsa temple, silver grass (eulsae) on oreum in Oct. Beautiful but requires a flight and is more resort/nature than temple-town.

shibuya_analogs.verdict: Hongdae/Yeonnam-dong: best match for Shibuya's youth energy, buskers, neon, karaoke (noraebang), purikura-style photo booths, late-night bars; Yeonnam adds Shimokitazawa-like side streets.
Myeongdong: densest neon + shopping + street-food stalls at night; touristy (like Shibuya Center-gai), easy to combine with Euljiro nogari alley and Namsan Tower.
Seongsu: closer to Daikanyama/Harajuku Cat Street than Shibuya; pop-up stores, converted factories, cafes. Lively daytime, quieter at night.
Gangnam Station: the literal big-crossing, office-crowd, glass-tower Shibuya look (plus COEX/Starfield Library nearby); less character on foot.
Busan Seomyeon: Busan's downtown neon/nightlife hub with Jeonpo cafe street and dwaeji gukbap alley; a smaller-scale Shibuya, good if staying in Busan.

izu_ryokan_analogs.verdict: Ragung (Gyeongju): hanok hotel where suites have private outdoor stone baths in a walled courtyard plus Korean set dinner. Closest single-property ryokan analog, but its website domain no longer resolves (Oct 2026); confirm it is operating before planning.
Paradise Hotel Busan + Cimer spa: Haeundae hot-spring water, outdoor ocean-view hot spring pools and Korean jjimjil rooms; Western rooms but the best 'onsen by the sea' feel (Izu-like).
Ananti at Busan Cove (Gijang): resort with Water House hot-spring bath/pools facing the sea, 10 min from Haedong Yonggungsa; Cabin S takes 3 adults (+KRW 50,000 extra bed).
Rakkojae Seoul (Bukchon): boutique hanok with ondol floor bedding, mud-sauna/bath, traditional dinner option. Ryokan-like hospitality in the city; small rooms.
Hurshimchung at Hotel Nongshim (Busan Dongnae Oncheon): huge public hot-spring bath (largest in Asia per Wikipedia) - like a big Izu onsen bathhouse; stay at Hotel Nongshim for direct access.
Sokcho Cheoksan hot springs / Seorak hot-spring resorts: classic Korean onsen-town feel after a Seoraksan foliage hike; dated facilities.
Suanbo (Chungju) and Onyang (Asan): historic royal hot-spring towns, now dated and old-fashioned; only worth it if routing through. Onyang is a 35-min KTX/1h40 subway from Seoul.

places.name: Haeundae Blueline Park (Beach Train & Sky Capsule)
places.summary: 4.8 km former Donghae Nambu Line rail along the cliffs between Mipo and Songjeong, converted into a slow sea-view Beach Train (all seats face the sea) and an elevated two-car Sky Capsule track (Mipo-Cheongsapo, 2 km, about 30 min one way).
places.why: Direct analog to Kamakura's Enoden coastal train: little train, sea on one side, small fishing harbors (Cheongsapo, Gudeokpo) and cafes at each stop.
places.autumn_note: October is off-season pricing/hours; clear autumn air and sunset light over Haeundae. Sky Capsule Oct hours 08:30-18:30.
places.time_needed: 2-3 hours including a walk around Cheongsapo
places.hours: Sky Capsule (Mar/Apr/Oct): 08:30-18:30. Beach Train roughly 09:30-19:00 in autumn (check traintime page).
places.closed: Operates daily; suspended in strong wind/rain.
places.cost_note: Official 2026 fares: Sky Capsule per capsule 2p 50,000 / 3p 55,000 (18,300 pp) / 4p 60,000 one way. Beach Train one-way 8,000-10,000 (by station), 2 rides 14,000, all-day pass 16,000 pp. For 3: capsule Mipo->Cheongsapo 55,000 + Beach Train back 3x10,000 = ~85,000 total.
places.booking: bluelinepark.com (English site); Sky Capsule sells out on weekends - book online ahead (reported release every Tuesday 07:00 for 4 weeks ahead). Foreign cards generally accepted; Klook/KKday also resell.
places.tips: Do Sky Capsule one way (Mipo->Cheongsapo) and walk/Beach Train onward to Cheongsapo Daritdol Skywalk and Songjeong. Pair with Haedong Yonggungsa (taxi 10 min from Songjeong).

places.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
places.summary: Rare seaside Buddhist temple on rocks above the waves, with a sea-facing Haesu Gwaneum Daebul statue, stone lanterns and the 108-step approach.
places.why: The most Kamakura/Enoshima-like temple moment in Korea: temple + surf in one frame. Busy like Hase-dera.
places.autumn_note: Mild October weather; go at opening to avoid tour buses; sunrise from the rocks is the classic shot.
places.tips: Bus 181/1001 or taxi from Haeundae/Songjeong (~15-20 min). Combine with Ananti Cove or Gijang Daebyeon harbor seafood lunch.

places.name: Cheongsapo & Daritdol Skywalk
places.summary: Small fishing village with twin red/white lighthouses, grilled-clam shacks and a glass-floor skywalk over the sea; a stop on the Blueline Beach Train.
places.why: Feels like Koshigoe/Shichirigahama on the Enoden: small port, sea views, slow cafes.
places.autumn_note: Good sunset spot; grilled shellfish (jogae-gui) season.
places.tips: Jogae-gui (grilled shellfish) shacks: roughly KRW 50,000-70,000 for a platter for 2-3 (unverified 2026).

places.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
places.summary: White-walled houses and narrow lanes on a sea cliff with a coastal walking path below (Jeoryeong coastal road).
places.why: Small-streets-by-the-sea charm (Kamakura/Enoshima back alleys) with cafes facing anchored ships; calmer than Gamcheon.
places.autumn_note: Afternoon light; pair with Taejongdae cliffs and Yeongdo eomuk (fish cake) shops.
places.tips: Residents live here - keep quiet. Samjin Eomuk HQ is nearby in Bongnae-dong.

places.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
places.summary: Pastel hillside refugee-era village turned art village with staircases, murals and harbor views.
places.why: Colorful hillside lanes; more Instagram than temple-town but fills the 'charming streets' itch.
places.autumn_note: Fine in any weather; very crowded weekends.
places.tips: Go early; combine with Jagalchi Market lunch.

places.name: Naksansa Temple
places.summary: Temple founded 671 by Uisang on a seaside bluff: 16 m Haesu Gwaneum statue facing the East Sea, Uisangdae pavilion clinging to rocks, Hongnyeonam hermitage over a sea cave.
places.why: The most atmospheric 'temple by the sea' in Korea - Kamakura's Hase-dera + Enoshima cliffs. Offers templestay.
places.autumn_note: Same trip as Seoraksan peak foliage (typically mid-late Oct). Uisangdae sunrise is famous.
places.cost_note: Cultural heritage admission fees for Jogye temples were abolished in May 2023; parking fee may apply.
places.tips: From Sokcho ~25 min by bus/taxi. Hajodae pavilion (Yangyang) is a nearby bonus seaside pavilion.

places.name: Abai Village & gaetbae raft
places.summary: Sandbar village built by North Korean refugees in 1950-51; reached by a hand-pulled cable raft (gaetbae) across the harbor channel; known for Abai sundae and Hamgyeong-style naengmyeon.
places.why: Small-streets fishing-village charm with a quirky little ride - a Kamakura-like half day with Naksansa.
places.autumn_note: October is squid/fish season on the east coast; Sokcho market at its liveliest.
places.tips: Eat at Dancheon Sikdang (Abai sundae) then cross to Sokcho Jungang Market for Manseok dakgangjeong.

places.name: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market
places.summary: Covered market with a basement live-fish hall (hoe to go) and famous dakgangjeong (sweet crispy chicken), squid sundae, hotteok.
places.why: Like Kamakura's Komachi-dori snack crawl but seafood-heavy.
places.autumn_note: Fall: squid, sea bream, gizzard shad in the basement; red snow crab (hongge) available.
places.cost_note: Pay per item; dakgangjeong box ~KRW 20,000-25,000 (2025 range).
places.tips: Buy hoe in the basement and eat on the Cheongcho lake promenade or at your hotel.

places.name: Gangneung: Anmok Coffee Street, Gyeongpo & Ojukheon
places.summary: Beachfront line of roasteries (Korea's coffee capital), Gyeongpo lake and beach, Ojukheon (birthplace of Yulgok and Sin Saimdang, Joseon hanok).
places.why: Small seaside city with culture: closest to Kamakura's mix of beach + heritage houses, plus tofu village (Chodang) like Kamakura's local specialties.
places.autumn_note: Gangneung Coffee Festival is traditionally in October (2026 dates not verified). Gyeongpo lake reeds and Ojukheon black bamboo in fall light.
places.tips: Gangneung is 1h50 from Seoul by KTX; Jeongdongjin (station on the beach) 15 min by train.

places.name: Tongyeong: Dongpirang mural village & Hallyeosu cable car
places.summary: Harbor town ('Naples of Korea') with hillside mural lanes above Jungang market, cable car up Mireuksan over the Hallyeo archipelago.
places.why: Seaside small-streets and harbor food culture; strongest for food (oysters, chungmu gimbap).
places.autumn_note: Tongyeong oyster harvest begins around October (peak Dec-Feb).
places.time_needed: 1 day (2h10 by bus from Busan Seobu terminal)
places.closed: Cable car closed some Mondays/maintenance days (verify).
places.cost_note: Cable car round trip ~KRW 17,000 adult (pre-2026 price; verify).
places.tips: Better as a south-coast detour than a core stop on a 8-night first trip.

places.name: Yeosu Hyangiram Hermitage
places.summary: Hermitage wedged into a sea cliff with rock tunnels, facing the sunrise over the South Sea.
places.why: Very Kamakura/Enoshima - cliff temple above the sea; Yeosu adds night harbor pojangmacha and sea cable car.
places.time_needed: 2 hours (+40 min drive from Yeosu city)
places.cost_note: Hermitage entry ~KRW 2,000 (pre-2026; may now be free).
places.tips: Out of the way for a Seoul-Gyeongju-Busan route (Yeosu-Expo is 2h50 by KTX from Seoul).

places.name: Seogwipo (Jeju) coast & Olle trail 6/7
places.summary: Seaside town with waterfalls (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon), Lee Jung-seob art street, Olle market, coastal cliff walks.
places.why: Seaside + small-town streets, but more Izu/Okinawa than Kamakura; adds black pork.
places.autumn_note: October silver grass (eulsae) on Saebyeol/Ttarabi oreum; tangerines start ripening.
places.tips: Rank last for this trip: costs a flight day.

places.name: Hongdae & Yeonnam-dong
places.summary: University district with busking on Eoulmadang-ro, clubs, noraebang, photo booths, character shops; Yeonnam-dong's Gyeongui Line Forest Park for cafes and bars.
places.why: Best Shibuya analog: youthful street energy, neon, late nights. Yeonnam = Shimokitazawa.
places.autumn_note: Friday/Saturday nights busiest; pleasant outdoor drinking weather in October.
places.cost_note: Free to wander; noraebang ~KRW 15,000-30,000/hour per room.
places.tips: Hongik Univ. Station (Line 2/AREX) - direct AREX from Incheon Airport.

places.name: Myeongdong night street food + Euljiro Nogari Alley
places.summary: Neon shopping streets with evening food stalls; 10 min walk to Euljiro 3-ga's nogari (dried pollock) beer alley with plastic tables on the street.
places.why: Shibuya-level crowds/neon (Myeongdong) + Omoide Yokocho-style drinking alley (Euljiro).
places.autumn_note: Outdoor beer-alley season ends as nights get cold in November - late October is ideal.
places.closed: Nogari alley bars often closed Sundays
places.cost_note: Street snacks KRW 4,000-10,000; nogari + beer ~KRW 10,000-15,000 pp.
places.tips: Myeongdong food is pricier/touristy; Gwangjang Market is better food value.

places.name: Seongsu-dong
places.summary: Former shoe-factory district of brick warehouses turned into cafes, pop-up stores, Korean designer brands; Seoul Forest park adjacent.
places.why: Harajuku/Daikanyama trendy-shopping analog rather than Shibuya crowds.
places.autumn_note: Seoul Forest ginkgo/zelkova foliage late Oct-early Nov.
places.booking: Popular pop-ups may need on-site waitlist (often via KakaoTalk).
places.tips: Combine with Born & Bred (Majang) or Seoul Forest.

places.name: Gangnam Station & COEX Starfield Library
places.summary: Office-tower crossing district with massive foot traffic, big screens, restaurants; COEX Mall's two-story bookshelf atrium and K-pop square screens nearby.
places.why: Visually closest to Shibuya Scramble (towers, screens, crowds) but less street-level fun.
places.tips: Sushi Kanesaka Seoul is in the InterContinental Parnas next to COEX.

places.name: Seomyeon & Jeonpo Cafe Street
places.summary: Busan's downtown: neon streets, underground shopping, clubs, dwaeji gukbap alley, and Jeonpo's hip cafe street in old hardware-shop lanes.
places.why: Busan's Shibuya; smaller but with better pork-soup culture.
places.tips: Seomyeon dwaeji gukbap alley; Choryang milmyeon a few stops away.

places.name: Hurshimchung Spa (Dongnae Oncheon)
places.summary: Huge hot-spring bathhouse (opened 1991, 4,300 m2, capacity 3,000) run by Hotel Nongshim: alkaline spring water 45-56C, many pools, saunas, outdoor bath, jjimjil area.
places.why: The 'big onsen' half of the Izu ryokan experience; Dongnae has been a hot-spring town since Silla times (Japan analog: Atami).
places.autumn_note: Outdoor bath feels best on cool October evenings.
places.cost_note: Adult admission historically ~KRW 15,000-20,000 (not verified for 2026); Hotel Nongshim guests get discounts/free entry depending on package.
places.tips: Oncheonjang Station (Line 1). Gender-separated nude bathing like onsen; tattoos generally tolerated more than Japan. Dongnae Oncheon free public foot bath nearby.

places.name: Spaland Centum City
places.summary: Upscale hot-spring jjimjilbang inside Shinsegae Centum City with natural spring baths, outdoor foot bath and themed sauna rooms.
places.why: Most accessible jjimjilbang experience for first-timers; clean and well signed.
places.cost_note: Pre-2026 price ~KRW 20,000-23,000 weekdays, higher weekends; website down when checked Oct 2026 - verify it is operating.

lodging.name: Ragung Hanok Hotel
lodging.room_for_3: Hanok suites with ondol floor bedding plus a bed; private outdoor stone bath in each walled courtyard; family suites sleep 3-4.
lodging.price_note: Estimate only from pre-2026 rates (roughly KRW 400k-800k for a suite); could not verify 2026. The official domain ragung.co.kr does not resolve (checked Oct 6 2026) - confirm it is still operating via Naver Map / booking sites.
lodging.highlights: Closest Izu-ryokan analog: private open-air bath, hanok courtyard, Korean set meals (hanjeongsik) served on site; 15 min from Bulguksa.
lodging.drawbacks: Possible closure/rebrand; dated facilities in recent reviews; car/taxi needed.

lodging.name: Paradise Hotel Busan (Cimer spa)
lodging.room_for_3: Deluxe twin + extra bed, or family/suite rooms; ocean-view rooms on Haeundae Beach.
lodging.price_note: Estimate (unverified 2026): ocean-view twin with extra bed typically KRW 400k-550k weekday, 600k+ Saturday. Cimer hot-spring spa often included or discounted for guests.
lodging.highlights: Natural Haeundae hot-spring outdoor pools facing the sea (the 'onsen by the ocean' moment), Korean jjimjil rooms; walk to Blueline Park Mipo station (10 min).
lodging.drawbacks: Western hotel, not a ryokan; pricey on weekends.
lodging.booking: busanparadisehotel.co.kr or OTAs; foreigners can book.

lodging.name: Ananti at Busan Cove
lodging.room_for_3: Cabin S (70 m2, 1 bedroom) - standard 2, max 3 with extra bed KRW 50,000; or connecting rooms for 4.
lodging.price_note: Room-rate estimate (unverified 2026); extra-bed fee KRW 50,000 confirmed on official site.
lodging.highlights: Water House hot-spring bath/pools facing the sea, bookstore Ananti Town, coastal walking path to Haedong Yonggungsa.
lodging.drawbacks: Expensive; 30 min taxi to central Haeundae.

lodging.name: Hotel Nongshim (Hurshimchung)
lodging.room_for_3: Deluxe twin + extra bed, or Korean-style ondol room (floor bedding).
lodging.price_note: Estimate (unverified 2026); packages often include Hurshimchung entry.
lodging.highlights: Direct access to Hurshimchung hot spring; ondol rooms; cheapest way to sleep in an onsen-town setting.
lodging.drawbacks: Older hotel; 30-40 min subway to Haeundae/Nampo.

lodging.name: Rakkojae Seoul
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol floor-bedding rooms; larger rooms sleep 3.
lodging.price_note: Estimate (unverified 2026). Website rkj.co.kr had an SSL error when checked.
lodging.highlights: 130-year-old hanok, mud (hwangto) sauna/bath, traditional breakfast and optional hanjeongsik dinner, tea in the courtyard - the most ryokan-like hospitality in Seoul.
lodging.drawbacks: Small rooms, shared or compact bathrooms in some rooms; floor sleeping.

lodging.name: Rakkojae Andong Hahoe
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms with floor bedding for 3.
lodging.highlights: Hanok inside UNESCO Hahoe village with hinoki/wood bath and jjimjil; Andong hanjeongsik-style dinner.
lodging.drawbacks: Andong is off the Seoul-Gyeongju-Busan line (but KTX-Eum Seoul-Andong ~2h).

lodging.name: Seongyojang Hanok Stay
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol rooms in a 300-year-old aristocratic manor; some rooms fit 3-4.
lodging.highlights: Authentic yangban manor with lotus pavilion; affordable heritage stay near Gyeongpo/Chodang.

lodging.name: Hanwha Resort Seorak Sorano + Seorak Waterpia
lodging.room_for_3: Condo-style family rooms with kitchenette (bed + floor bedding).
lodging.price_note: Estimate; late October is Seorak foliage peak - weekends spike and sell out.
lodging.highlights: Seorak hot-spring water park/spa (outdoor hot spring baths with Ulsanbawi view), 15 min to Seoraksan.

food.name: Sosuheon
food.type: sushi omakase - high (2 Michelin stars 2026, new)
food.booking: Phone +82 10-9694-3368 (self-managed; Korean-speaking; ask hotel concierge). 8 seats.
food.why: Seoul's only 2-star sushi counter (2026), in a hanok - the closest to a top Tokyo omakase. Chef Park Kyung-jae (ex-Sushi Kojima). Dinner ~KRW 500,000 (Korean report; lunch price not found).

food.name: Sushi Kanesaka Seoul
food.type: sushi omakase - high (1 Michelin star 2026, new)
food.booking: Phone 02-559-7627 or hotel site; all seats pre-booked; 9 seats. Lunch 12:00 (LO 12:30), dinner 18:00 (LO 20:00); Saturday dinner two seatings 17:30/20:00.
food.why: Official 2026 prices: lunch KRW 230,000-280,000, dinner KRW 330,000-380,000 (depends on chef). Edomae lineage of Ginza Kanesaka; hotel booking is easiest for foreigners.

food.name: Sushi Matsumoto
food.why: Japanese chef Mizuho Matsumoto (ex-Sushi Cho); traditional Edomae with strong tsumami. 2026 price not found (₩₩₩₩ tier; expect ~KRW 250k+ lunch / 350k+ dinner).

food.name: Sushi Cho (The Westin Josun Seoul)
food.booking: Westin Josun website or phone; English-speaking hotel staff.
food.why: Classic hotel sushi counter, easiest high-end booking for foreigners. Reported dinner omakase KRW 340,000, lunch ~KRW 140,000+ (aggregator, date unclear).

food.name: Sushi Chohi
food.why: Value counter: lunch from KRW 45,000, dinner from KRW 110,000 (2026 article).

food.name: Sushi Jinsu
food.why: Lunch omakase KRW 45,000 with free corkage (2026 blog).

food.name: Sushi Sora (Gwanghwamun / Mapo / Daechi / Seocho)
food.why: Reliable entry-level counter: lunch KRW 50,000-60,000, dinner KRW 100,000-110,000 (list date unclear; likely 2024-25).

food.name: Iwa
food.why: Chef holds a patent for fish aging; best value Michelin-listed omakase in Busan. Lunch ~KRW 80,000; dinner ₩₩₩.

food.name: Sushi Nee (L7 Haeundae)
food.why: Lunch KRW 60,000, dinner KRW 110,000; parties up to 7 - easy for 3.

food.name: Sushi Ima
food.why: One of Busan's top sushi counters; dinner KRW 180,000.

food.name: Mori
food.booking: Phone +82 51-731-9889 (CatchTable also reported). Dinner Tue-Fri 19:00, Sat-Sun 17:00; closed Mon.
food.why: Kaiseki by a Japan-trained Korean chef and his Japanese wife using Busan seafood - the best substitute for an Izu ryokan dinner. Prix fixe ~KRW 250,000 (reported).

food.name: Born and Bred
food.type: hanu (Korean beef) omakase / BBQ - Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best 2026 #56
food.booking: Basement chef's tasting via CatchTable, 2-3 months ahead; phone +82 2-2294-5005. Closed Tue.
food.why: The sushi-omakase experience translated to hanu: counter, chef-paced cuts. Chef's tasting KRW 380,000; 2F a la carte ~KRW 70,000/150g sirloin.

food.name: Umok
food.why: Counter hanu omakase KRW 99,000 (room 180,000) - Dec 2024 prices, likely higher now.

food.name: Mingles
food.booking: CatchTable Global (opens ~1 month ahead, sells out fast) or restaurant-mingles.com; +82 2-515-7306. Closed Sun-Mon.
food.why: Korea's only 3-star; jang (fermented sauce) driven Korean tasting - the kaiseki-level Korean meal. Lunch KRW 320,000 since 1 Mar 2026; dinner reported ~KRW 420,000.

food.name: Onjium
food.booking: Phone +82 2-6952-0024 (self-managed). Michelin lists Tue-Fri lunch 12:00-15:00; closed Sat-Mon. Cash only per Michelin listing.
food.why: Research-institute restaurant reviving royal cuisine with palace views - the most 'cultural' Korean tasting. Lunch reported ~KRW 140,000, dinner ~KRW 260,000 (third-party).

food.name: Bicena
food.why: Korean tasting 81 floors up - pair with Seoul Sky. Lunch ~KRW 170,000 (third-party).

food.name: Kwonsooksoo
food.why: Traditional-leaning Korean fine dining with jang and banchan focus; from ~KRW 200,000+ (third-party).

food.name: Le DORER
food.why: Busan's newly starred Korean tasting menu (chef Kim Chang-uk); price not verified.

food.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
food.type: hoe (raw fish) market - buy downstairs, eat upstairs
food.why: Tsukiji-style experience: pick live fish, have it sliced, eat at a 2F restaurant (sangcharim setting fee ~KRW 5,000-6,000 pp). Aug 2026 farmed flatfish KRW 22,800/kg wholesale; seasonal moksum platters ~KRW 50,000 for 2. In Oct: daeha prawns, kkotge, jeoneo.

food.name: Jagalchi Market
food.why: Korea's biggest fish market: buy on 1F, eat on 2F (table fee ~KRW 5,000 pp). Hoe platter for two ~KRW 30,000-60,000 (2026). Overcharging controversies in 2024-25 - agree price per kg first; go past the first row of stalls.

food.name: Millak Fishermen's Live Fish Market
food.why: Buy fish on 1F, eat upstairs facing Gwangan Bridge's light show - the best hoe night in Busan. Flatfish ~KRW 30,000/kg; 2-person set ~KRW 40,000-45,000; setting fee ~KRW 6,000 pp (recent blogs).

food.name: Daebyeon Port / Gijang Market
food.type: seafood (anchovy, sea-squirt, grilled eel, Gijang snow crab tanks)
food.why: Small port near Haedong Yonggungsa for hoe and grilled kkomjangeo (hagfish) - fishing-village lunch like Kamakura's Koshigoe shirasu. Gijang market sells (mostly imported/red) crab year-round.

food.name: Gwangjang Market (bindaetteok, yukhoe, mayak gimbap)
food.why: Seoul's essential food market: mung-bean pancakes (Soonhee-ne ~KRW 5,000-6,000), beef tartare (Buchon Yukhoe, Michelin Bib), makgeolli. Avoid stall price-gouging (some 2023-24 controversies).

food.name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
food.why: Cult samgyeopsal/ribs over briquettes - the Korean BBQ benchmark.

food.name: Mongtan
food.booking: On-site waitlist (long queues; arrive before opening)
food.why: Most famous galbi BBQ in Seoul (straw-fire smoked ujik-galbi). Price estimate.

food.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley / Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha
food.why: Plastic-stool tent bars - the Korean answer to yokocho/izakaya alleys.

food.name: Ssangdungi Dwaeji Gukbap
food.why: Busan's signature comfort food. Michelin Bib alternatives: Jeongjitgan (Saha-gu). Price estimate ~KRW 10,000-12,000.

food.name: Gaegeum Milmyeon
food.why: Classic milmyeon (Michelin Bib in past editions). Price estimate.

food.name: Samjin Eomuk (Yeongdo flagship)
food.why: Busan fish-cake institution since 1953; croquette-style eomuk. Pair with Huinnyeoul village.

food.name: BIFF Square ssiat hotteok stalls
food.why: Fried pancake stuffed with brown sugar and seeds - Busan's iconic street snack, next to Jagalchi.

food.name: Hwangnam Bread (main shop)
food.why: Since 1939; Gyeongju's omiyage (like Kamakura's hato sable). Box of 20 ~KRW 20,000 (pre-2026).

food.name: Daereungwon ssambap street
food.type: ssambap (lettuce-wrap rice set with many banchan)
food.why: Gyeongju's set meal of wraps, banchan and bulgogi - a casual hanjeongsik. Price estimate KRW 15,000-20,000.

food.name: Gyori Gimbap
food.why: Famous egg-heavy gimbap near Woljeonggyo bridge.

tips: Booking sushi/hansik as foreigners: CatchTable Global app takes foreign cards and no Korean phone number; many top counters (Sosuheon, Sushi Matsumoto, Onjium, Mori, Iwa) manage bookings by phone only - ask your hotel concierge to call, or DM on Instagram.
Expect strict no-show rules: typical 50% charge within 3 days and 100% within 24 h; deposits charged at booking on CatchTable.
Lunch omakase is 30-50% cheaper than dinner at the same counter (e.g., Sushi Kanesaka Seoul lunch KRW 230k vs dinner 330k).
Korean sushi tiers in 2026: entry KRW 50k-100k, mid 100k-200k, high-end 200k-500k per person (dinner).

Best Izu-ryokan substitute is usually two pieces: an ocean-view hot-spring hotel (Paradise Busan/Ananti) + a kaiseki-like dinner (Mori in Busan, Mingles/Onjium/Bicena in Seoul) - Korea has few true all-in-one ryokans.

Hoe markets: buy fish by weight on the ground floor, then pay a per-person setting fee (KRW ~5,000-6,000) upstairs plus extra for maeuntang spicy fish stew; confirm the price per kg before the fish is killed.

For the 'Kamakura day' do: Blueline Sky Capsule Mipo->Cheongsapo (morning) - Daritdol Skywalk - Beach Train to Songjeong - taxi to Haedong Yonggungsa - Gijang/Daebyeon hoe lunch - Ananti Cove or back to Haeundae.
Pair Naksansa + Abai Village + Sokcho market with a Seoraksan foliage day; Seorak hot-spring resorts make it ryokan-ish.
Gangneung is the easiest Seoul day trip that scratches the seaside-town itch (KTX ~1h50 from Seoul Station).
warnings: Ragung (Gyeongju) - official domain ragung.co.kr does not resolve as of Oct 6 2026; verify operating status before relying on it.
Spaland Centum City website was unreachable when checked; confirm operation.
Daegae (snow crab) is out of its domestic season in October - crab you see is imported or red snow crab.
Jagalchi and Gwangjang markets had price-gouging controversies in 2024-25; ask prices first.
Sky Capsule weekend slots sell out; book as soon as the 4-week window opens.
Many omakase counters are closed Sunday/Monday (e.g., Mingles closed Sun-Mon, Sushi Matsumoto Sun-Mon, Mori Mon, Onjium Sat-Mon) - plan Sun Oct 18/Mon Oct 19 accordingly.

Some third-party Michelin roundups (e.g., koreaexperience.com) misstate 2026 star counts; the official list: Mingles is the sole 3-star; Sosuheon is the only 2-star sushi; Sushi Matsumoto and Sushi Kanesaka 1-star; Mori 1-star in Busan.
